why:
ADOPT-BOUNDED replacement for upstream's throwing constructor: a node that failed to come up records the failure and answers `false` here. The SPELLING is upstream's own (`rclcpp::ok()` asks the same question of the process), which is why this is `ok()` and not an invented `is_healthy()`. It is weaker than a throw and the weakening is only safe if it is loud: the generated entry checks it and halts naming the node (RFC-0044 Q2), and a hand-written `main` must check it -- documented in the book, because the compiler cannot force it. `is_valid()` is the older nano-ros spelling of the same bit and stays as a forwarder.

phase-427 W4 — it answers for the LATCH as well as for creation now. `ComponentNode` held a 24-byte `has_error_`/`error_what_`/`error_code_` latch that a failed `create_*` wrote after a successful open; merging it means `ok()` is `initialized_ && !has_error_`, which is what the entry's post-construct check has always MEANT. Those 24 bytes are UNCONDITIONAL on every node and deliberately not behind the hosted block: this is the error channel a `-fno-exceptions` target has instead of a throwing constructor, so a latch reachable only on a hosted target would leave the firmware case -- the one that cannot throw -- with no channel at all. Measured cost: `sizeof(nros::Node)` 200 -> 224, identical hosted and freestanding.
